notes: kol səbîbōtênû is rendered by the relative frame all that is round about us; that is round about belongs to the adverbial noun's own rendering rather than being an added subordinator, since sābîb is what the phrase turns on and the corpus reads round about headed on round.
In the grass of the field the rectum is arthrous, so nothing is fronted and the construct takes a supplied the while the article takes the the before its own word (rule 29).
The bāʿēt hahîʾ phrase writes two article morphemes and one determiner: the demonstrative takes that and both articles are unrepresented (rules 41, 47).
